title: Direct engine demonstration — record pipeline
summary: The minimal direct engine path: a self-contained record-processing pipeline compiled from FW_Group, FW_PermutR and a three-link nested-brace chain, judged by an exact differential oracle. No external checkout, no network, standard library only.

source.revision_resolution: Moves with the Framework checkout; the engine revision reported by `bundle_run.py architecture` identifies it.

lifecycle.start: none — the SUT is a library the candidate imports; there is no server to start
lifecycle.stop: none — no process outlives a candidate

determinism.reset: Each candidate is an independent subprocess building its own pipeline from a fixed integer corpus; no state survives a candidate.
determinism.seed: No seed needed: the corpus is a module constant and every stage is a total, deterministic function.

oracle.description: Three independent layers: a compiled closure-tree evaluator versus a separately written recursive interpreter; a structural output-length bound computed without executing anything; and an exact service contract (non-empty, non-decreasing, in band) that alone may report a domain failure.
oracle.independence: The two evaluators are deliberately not factored together — the duplication IS the oracle. test_the_differential_oracle_is_not_vacuous seeds a defect into one and requires the other to catch it, so a passing differential check is evidence rather than a tautology.

intentional_defects.description: Sorting and then negating produces a descending stream that violates the declared service contract. Neither grouped module can violate it alone: both are monotone.

cleanup: python generator_trunk/bundle_run.py cleanup <run-dir>; runtime output lives under /tmp/fw_work and never in the source tree.
caveats: Bounded at 8 candidates by design: it is the minimal proof of higher-order composition, not a scale or coverage showcase.
Uses trusted-local because the candidate fragments are reviewed and checked in; generated candidates must not reuse this row.
